channel.title: The daily tape · compute.world
channel.description: Two answers to the same grid constraint landed between Sunday and Monday. In Arkansas the tenant pays: Entergy Arkansas announced a second phase of service for Google's West Memphis campus, with Google covering about $600 million of battery, substation and transmission investment plus a 440 MW solar PPA, pending Arkansas PSC approval and an expected 2028 in-service date. Where no tenant pays, governments ration: Denmark's executive order 892 took effect on 19 October and places data centres in the lowest of four priority categories when grid capacity is short, and Israel's Electricity Authority backed a 200 MW cap per new data center, about 1,000 MW of new large connections and NIS 2 million per MW guarantees after 27,000 MW of requests. Goldman Sachs counts 86 data center projects canceled or significantly delayed since January, 76 of them tied to local opposition, and calls power 'probably the forever bottleneck'. Capital is still chasing sites with power: Bloomberg and CNBC report Anthropic is in talks for a second 460 MW building at Nscale's Monarch campus in West Virginia worth about $45 billion, even as investors push back on Nscale's roughly $30 billion IPO target and Korea's Elice fell about 30% on its KOSDAQ debut. On the public silicon tape all six venues returned HTTP 200: 71 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW. CoreWeave's list held at $6.16 for H100 even as Goldman's upgrade note cites CoreWeave price increases of 25% in July and 10% in October, which sit in contracts, not the public page.

item.title: Compute brief - 20 October 2026
item.description: Two answers to the same grid constraint landed between Sunday and Monday. In Arkansas the tenant pays: Entergy Arkansas announced a second phase of service for Google's West Memphis campus, with Google covering about $600 million of battery, substation and transmission investment plus a 440 MW solar PPA, pending Arkansas PSC approval and an expected 2028 in-service date. Where no tenant pays, governments ration: Denmark's executive order 892 took effect on 19 October and places data centres in the lowest of four priority categories when grid capacity is short, and Israel's Electricity Authority backed a 200 MW cap per new data center, about 1,000 MW of new large connections and NIS 2 million per MW guarantees after 27,000 MW of requests. Goldman Sachs counts 86 data center projects canceled or significantly delayed since January, 76 of them tied to local opposition, and calls power 'probably the forever bottleneck'. Capital is still chasing sites with power: Bloomberg and CNBC report Anthropic is in talks for a second 460 MW building at Nscale's Monarch campus in West Virginia worth about $45 billion, even as investors push back on Nscale's roughly $30 billion IPO target and Korea's Elice fell about 30% on its KOSDAQ debut. On the public silicon tape all six venues returned HTTP 200: 71 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW. CoreWeave's list held at $6.16 for H100 even as Goldman's upgrade note cites CoreWeave price increases of 25% in July and 10% in October, which sit in contracts, not the public page. Countries: United States: Entergy Arkansas phase 2 for Google West Memphis: Google covers about $600 million of batteries (1,400 MWh), substation and two 230 kV lines plus a 440 MW solar PPA; APSC approval pending, 2028 in service (Wire, 19 Oct). Anthropic in talks for a second 460 MW Nscale Monarch building in West Virginia, about $45 billion (Signal). Denmark: Executive order 892 in force 19 Oct: data centres are category 4 of 4 for constrained grid capacity; operators can refuse requests that displace higher priorities; 3 MW+ requests handled in regional rounds at least twice a year (Wire). Israel: Electricity Authority backs a 200 MW cap per new data center, about 1,000 MW of new large-DC connections on top of about 2,000 MW approved, NIS 2 million per MW guarantees; 27,000 MW was requested; three-week consultation next (Wire, 18 Oct). Malaysia: Aolani signs non-binding LOIs for up to 500 MW of AI data centre capacity from 2H 2027; projects up to 580 MW committed in Malaysia by 2027 versus about 80 MW in 2026 (Wire, 19 Oct).
